full_judgment:
Petitioner's Case 

 2. The petitioner's case as narrated in the writ petition as well as in the reply to the affidavit-in-opposition is as follows:— 

 Petitioner, SM Abdus Salam, is the Proprietor of M/s Shawon Enterprise. He is engaged in the business as Overseas Bank) exported commodities to Bangladeshi Importer, namely, M/s Seven Trade International (briefly stated as Seven Trade) and that on examination of the documents of Bhomra Customs Station, it was found that Indian Exporter BR International and Bangladeshi Importer MP International through L/C No. 0120915010312 dated 6-10-2015 issued by Social Islami Bank Limited (shortly, Social Bank) had released the aforesaid imported goods through petitioner as C&F Agent with false statement collusively and fraudulently. The petitioner gave reply to the said show cause notice on 12-5-2016 stating that he was engaged to release the imported goods of MP International of Bogra exported from BR International, West Bengal, India through L/C No. 0120915010312 dated 6-10-2015 issued by Social Bank, Bogra Branch, Bogra. But, the petitioner had no knowledge about the exporter Sheikh Saria or the importer Seven Trade. The Joint Com-missioner then heard the petitioner in-person. At the time of hearing, the petitioner submitted written statements on 3-8-2016 stating that he through proper documents released the raw cotton as' an authorized C&F Agent. Thereafter, the petitioner received the impugned order signed by the Joint Commissioner by suspending the petitioner's License allegedly for violating the provisions of section 2(ka) read with section 207 of the Customs Act, 1969 (shortly, the Customs Act) and rules 20 and 21 of the Rules. Prior to this incident, Bhuiyan Mafizur Rahman, a Customs Officer of Customs Station, Bhomra lodged a First Information Report with Satkhira Police Station on 18-8-2015 being Satkhira Police Station Case No. 25 dated 18-8-2016 under sections 420/406/467/468/471 of the Penal Code. Whereupon, a criminal case was started against the petitioner and the importer, which is still under investigation. The petitioner was enlarged on ad-interim bail in the said criminal case on 3-4-2017 by the High Court Division vide Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 13333 of 2017. In connection with the said criminal case, the show cause notice was issued by the Joint Commissioner to the petitioner. The impugned suspension order was passed on 9-8-2016 and till date, no departmental proceeding has been drawn up against the petitioner and therefore, the order of suspension for an indefinite period is malafide, arbitrary and liable to be struck down. 

 Respondent No. 1’s Case 

 3. Respondent No. 1, the Joint Commissioner, contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition controverting the statements made in the writ petition and supporting the impugned order. It has been stated that on the basis of a complain from Indian Exporter Sheikh Saria, an Inquiry Committee was duly formed by the customs authority for investigation into the allegations made by the said Indian Exporter. After investigation, the Inquiry Committee submitted a report. From the report, it was Found that the Exporter Sheikh Saria exported goods against five L/Cs being L/C Nos. 071603 31510160 dated 1-11-2015, 120915010312, 120915010312 and 120915010312 all dated 6-11-2015 and 0716033 15101 76 dated 19-11-2015 issued by Indian Overseas Bank, Hongkong to Bangladeshi Importer, Seven Trade. The Joint Commissioner, on the basis of secret information, came to know that the said goods were released through tempered and forged shipping documents, etc. by the petitioner. After scrutiny/verification of the register/information of Bhomra Customs Station ASYCUDA World along with other related documents, the Joint Commissioner also found that Indian Exporter, BR International, Kolkata, exported the goods through L/C No. 120915010312 dated 6-11-2015 issued by Social Bank to Bangladeshi Importer, MP International, Bogra. The petitioner was appointed by MP International for release of the goods. But the petitioner allegedly released the goods of another exporter and importer by tempering and forging the shipping documents. Thus, it is found that the petitioner has violated the provisions of rule 21 of the Rules. The License of the petitioner has been provisionally suspended under rule 20 of the Rules. Suspension of a license is not a punishment and it has been passed for completion of investigation of the criminal case by the police. In the circumstances, the rule is liable to be discharged. 

 4. Mr ABM Waliur Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, takes us through the writ petition, the reply to the affidavit-in-opposition, the connected materials on record and submits that an Officer of Customs, Customs Station, Bhomra lodged a first information report being Satkhira Police Station Case No. 25 dated 18-8-2017 against the petitioner and an importer, which is under investigation. He next submits that meanwhile, over the same subject matter, the Joint Commissioner issued a show cause notice upon the petitioner, the petitioner gave reply to the show cause notice and then the Joint Commissioner, upon hearing the petitioner, passed the impugned order of suspension of the License on 9-8-2016. He further submits that although suspension order was passed on 9-8-2016, but till date no proceeding has been drawn up by the customs authority against the petitioner relating to the License. He finally submits that the suspension order of the License for an indefinite period without drawing up any departmental proceeding relating to License is malafide, arbitrary and, as such, liable to be struck down. 

 5. In support of his submissions, Mr Khan has relied on the decision in the case of Bangladesh Livestock Research Institute vs Dr Md Jahangir Alam Khan, reported in 20 BLT (AD) 239. 

 6. In reply, Mr AHM Ziauddin, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the Joint Commissioner (respondent No. 1), takes us through the affidavit-in-opposition and contends that the petitioner'' Customs House Agent License was suspended for violation of the provisions of rule 21 of the Rules. He next contends that there is no provision in the Rules within which an investigation has to be completed or the period for which a Customs House Agent License may remain suspended. He finally contends that the police has not completed the investigation of the case filed against the petitioner and therefore, the order of suspension cannot be said to be unlawful and the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 9. There is no dispute that a Customs Officer of Customs Station, Bhomra lodged Satkhira Police Station Case No. 25 dated 18-8-2016 against the petitioner and an importer under sections 420/406/467/468 and 471 of the Penal Code and that the said case is still under investigation it is not disputed that after filing of the aforesaid criminal case against the petitioner and another, the Joint Commissioner issued a show cause notice upon the petitioner for violating certain provisions of the Customs Act and the Rules made thereunder and that the petitioner gave reply to the said show cause notice. It is also admitted that upon hearing, the impugned order has been passed by the Joint Commissioner by suspending of the petitioner's Customs House Agent License on 9-8-2016 i.e. about one and half years back. Admittedly, till date, the Joint Commissioner failed to bring any departmental proceeding against the petitioner. The suspension order of the petitioner's license has not also been withdrawn by the authority concerned. 

 13. In the case repotted in 20 BLT (AD) 239, their lordships of the Appellate Division, in case of an order of suspension for an indefinite period, decided as under:— 

 14. In the instant case also, it transpires that though the License of the petitioner was suspended about one and half years back but, till date, the Customs Department after preliminary enquiry, failed to bring any departmental proceeding against the petitioner within the aforesaid period of about one and half years from the date of order of suspension of the License. Therefore, we are of the view that the principle set out in the above case is squarely applicable in this ease. 

 15. The learned Assistant Attorney-General fails to show us any prevision of law either in the Customs Act, 1969 or in the Rules that due to investigation of a criminal case, a license may remain suspended for an indefinite period. 

 16. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the opinion that the suspension order relating to the petitioner's Customs House Agent License for an indefinite period without bringing any departmental proceeding against the petitioner within about one and hall years is arbitrary and malafide.
